payload.explanation: Sharing food with someone who has none is one of the most direct and immediate acts of kindness.

payload.snippet: The school garden volunteers are trying to dig a large area and there are not enough tools.
options: Offer to take turns with the tools and help rotate the team
Grab a tool and keep it for the entire session
Stand and watch because you will just get in the way
Ask if the school can buy more tools before helping
payload.explanation: Coordinating a tool rotation is helping at an organisational level — more effective than individual effort alone.

payload.snippet: You see someone's pushchair roll away on a slope while the parent looks the other way.
options: Catch the pushchair calmly and bring it back straight away
Shout to the parent from far away
Let it go because someone else will catch it
Take a video in case it falls over
payload.explanation: Acting immediately when a child is at risk is always the right response.

payload.snippet: An elderly person at the doctor's surgery is struggling to open the heavy main door.
options: Hold the door open and wait for them to pass through
Let the door swing shut and walk through yourself
Open the door and walk straight in ahead of them
Watch from inside to see if they manage alone
payload.explanation: Holding a heavy door for someone is a simple act that costs nothing and matters a lot.

payload.snippet: Your friend is working on a creative project and asks for your honest feedback.
options: Give kind, specific and honest feedback
Say it is perfect even if it is not
Criticise every single thing harshly
Refuse to give feedback to avoid any conflict
payload.explanation: Kind and honest feedback is the most genuinely helpful response to someone asking for your opinion.

payload.snippet: The park litter bin is overflowing and rubbish has blown around the play area.
options: Pick up rubbish near you and put it in a bag or nearby bin
Add your own litter to the pile
Post a photo on social media complaining
Wait for the council to deal with it
payload.explanation: Picking up nearby litter costs nothing and immediately makes the space better for everyone.

payload.snippet: Your little sibling wants to play with the new toy you got for your birthday.
options: Let them play with it for a while
Lock the toy in your room
Tell them to get their own
Cry until they go away
payload.explanation: Sharing new things shows generosity even when it is hard.

payload.snippet: Two friends both want to be the leader in the group game at school today.
options: Suggest taking turns being the leader each round
Tell one friend they cannot play
Make everyone fight it out
Ask the teacher to decide for you
payload.explanation: Rotating leadership gives everyone a fair chance and keeps the game fun.

payload.snippet: You have extra coloured pens and your classmate has only a pencil for the art project.
options: Offer a few pens for them to use during the lesson
Show off all your pens to make them jealous
Keep all your pens in case you need every one
Only share if they give you something back
payload.explanation: Sharing supplies helps everyone do their best work.

payload.snippet: The family has one big bag of crisps to share between three children after school.
options: Split them into roughly equal portions for each person
Eat as many as you can before anyone else gets there
Only give the smallest portions to the younger ones
Wait for someone else to divide them up instead
payload.explanation: Equal portions are fair and stop arguments from starting.

payload.snippet: Your friend has a book you really want to read and you have a book they want to read.
options: Suggest swapping books for a week so you both get to read one
Demand they lend theirs without offering yours
Ask the library to get you the same book
Say nothing and wait to see if they offer first
payload.explanation: A book swap means both people get what they want with nothing lost.

payload.snippet: There is only one computer at the library and both you and a classmate need to finish homework.
options: Agree to split the time equally and set a timer
Refuse to move even when you have finished
Tell the librarian to make the classmate wait
Work very slowly so they do not get a turn
payload.explanation: Splitting time equally is fair and means both people get the help they need.

payload.snippet: A visiting cousin is staying for the week and wants to use your bedroom while your aunt and uncle use the guest room.
options: Welcome the cousin and share your space for the week
Refuse and make the cousin sleep in the lounge
Complain to your parent every day of the visit
Lock your room so they cannot touch your things
payload.explanation: Sharing your space for a short visit is a welcoming and generous thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your team has one water bottle left at the end of the sports session and several players are thirsty.
options: Make sure everyone gets a small sip in turn
Drink the most because you ran the furthest
Give it only to your best friend on the team
Pour it all out so no one has an advantage
payload.explanation: Sharing what is left fairly keeps the whole team comfortable.

payload.snippet: You are playing a video game and your friend is watching and asking if they can have a turn.
options: Finish the level and then hand the controller over
Keep playing for hours without offering a turn
Tell them to go and find their own game
Pause the game every minute to ask if they still want to play
payload.explanation: Finishing a natural stopping point then handing over is a fair and smooth way to share.

payload.snippet: Your friend brought a home-made cake to school to share with the class and it turned out much smaller than expected.
options: Take a small piece so there is enough for everyone
Take the largest piece because you got there first
Complain that the slices are not big enough
Ask for seconds before everyone has had their first
payload.explanation: Taking a small piece when supply is limited means everyone gets to enjoy some.

payload.snippet: The family is going on a long car journey and your sibling wants to control the music for the whole trip.
options: Suggest each person picks a song in turns
Put your own headphones in and ignore the problem
Demand to control the music yourself all trip
Ask your parent to pick the music so no one argues
payload.explanation: A turn-based system means everyone enjoys some of their favourite music on a long journey.

payload.snippet: You made a batch of biscuits and your neighbour mentioned they could smell them from next door.
options: Bring a few over to share with the neighbour
Keep every biscuit because you made them yourself
Tell the neighbour they should bake their own
Eat them all before anyone can ask for one
payload.explanation: Sharing home-baked food with neighbours is a warm and neighbourly thing to do.

payload.snippet: Your friend group has one shared umbrella at a rainy bus stop and there are five of you.
options: Huddle together under the umbrella as best you can
Keep the umbrella entirely for yourself
Give the umbrella to someone else and stand in the rain
Argue about who stands in the middle until the bus comes
payload.explanation: Huddling together is imperfect but it shares the limited shelter as fairly as possible.

payload.snippet: You have finished using the shared family laptop but your parent still needs it tonight.
options: Let your parent have it now you are finished
Keep the laptop open just in case you think of something
Ask to use it for one more hour after you said you were done
Hide the laptop so nobody else can use it tonight
payload.explanation: Returning shared items promptly when you are finished is considerate and fair.

payload.snippet: Your best friend is visiting and wants to play with your most special toy.
options: Let them play with it carefully while they visit
Lock the special toy away before they arrive
Show them the toy but say they cannot touch it
Say the toy is broken so they do not ask
payload.explanation: Trusting a close friend with something special shows real friendship.

payload.snippet: You found a large packet of sweets in the cupboard and no one else is around.
options: Wait and share them with the family later
Eat them all before anyone comes home
Hide some for yourself then share the rest
Tell everyone else the packet was already empty
payload.explanation: Waiting to share found treats is honest and fair to the whole family.

payload.snippet: Two children both want the window seat on the bus and the journey takes forty minutes.
options: Suggest twenty minutes each and set a phone timer
Sit in the window seat and refuse all negotiation
Ask the driver to settle the argument
Give in completely and sit in discomfort for the full trip
payload.explanation: A timer makes the split concrete and removes any argument about when the turn ends.

payload.snippet: Your class has been given one big pack of craft supplies to share across the whole afternoon.
options: Take only what you need for your project
Take a large share in case you need more later
Hide supplies under the desk so others cannot reach them
Use the supplies slowly so your pile lasts longer than others
payload.explanation: Taking only what you need leaves enough for everyone to complete their work.

payload.snippet: Your sibling has saved up pocket money to buy a game you both want to play.
options: Offer to contribute some of your own savings toward the joint purchase
Let them buy it alone then demand to use it whenever you want
Offer no money but insist on equal playing time
Wait until they buy it and ask permission each time
payload.explanation: Contributing toward a shared purchase makes ownership genuinely equal and fair.

payload.snippet: A classmate's packed lunch fell on the floor and all their food is now ruined at lunchtime.
options: Share part of your own lunch with them
Eat your own lunch and avoid eye contact
Tell the teacher and leave the problem with them
Offer one tiny piece and keep everything else
payload.explanation: Sharing part of your lunch ensures the classmate is not hungry for the rest of the school day.

payload.snippet: You keep pressing the snooze button and now you have only fifteen minutes to get ready for school.
options: Get up immediately and skip non-essential steps to be on time
Press snooze one more time and see what happens
Ask your parent to write a late note for school
Text your friend to say you are going to be late again
payload.explanation: Cutting non-essential steps when you have pressed snooze too many times is the quickest way to recover lost time.

payload.snippet: Your school uniform shirt is creased badly and the iron is already hot but you are running short on time.
options: Give it a quick iron on the most visible areas and move on
Wear the creased shirt and hope no one notices
Switch to a different shirt that is not part of the uniform
Ask your parent to iron it while you eat breakfast slowly
payload.explanation: A quick iron of the visible areas is the fastest fix that makes the biggest difference to appearance.

payload.snippet: The bathroom is occupied by your sibling and you have ten minutes before you need to leave.
options: Do what you can at the kitchen sink while you wait
Bang on the door repeatedly until they come out
Wait at the bathroom door doing nothing
Skip washing completely today
payload.explanation: Using an alternative space keeps your routine moving without creating conflict.

payload.snippet: You realise you have not done part of your homework while eating breakfast before school.
options: Pack the homework and do the missing part in the form room before registration
Stay home until it is done
Submit what you have and tell the teacher at the start of class
Copy a friend's work on the bus
payload.explanation: Arriving early to form room to finish homework is honest and still gets it submitted on time.

payload.snippet: It is the first cold morning of the autumn and you cannot find your school coat anywhere.
options: Check the last place you wore it and if you cannot find it quickly wear an extra layer
Go without any coat in the cold
Turn the house upside down and miss school
Ask your parent to drive you because of the coat
payload.explanation: Wearing an extra layer solves the cold problem even if the coat takes longer to find later.

payload.snippet: Your packed lunch fell off the counter and everything has spilled on the kitchen floor.
options: Quickly rinse or replace any salvageable items and pack the rest fresh if time allows
Leave the mess and go to school without lunch
Cry and refuse to go to school
Ask your parent to bring lunch to school later
payload.explanation: A quick rinse and repack recovers most of a dropped lunch in under two minutes.

payload.snippet: You feel very tired this morning because you stayed up too late last night.
options: Get up, eat breakfast, and walk to school briskly to wake up naturally
Stay home because you are tired
Text your friend to say you cannot cope today
Go back to sleep after breakfast
payload.explanation: Moving and eating breakfast activates the body even when sleep was short — the tiredness usually eases once you are outside.

payload.snippet: Your bus pass is missing and you are not sure if you have enough change for the fare.
options: Count your change now and plan to look for the pass tonight
Refuse to get on the bus without the pass
Ask a stranger on the bus to pay for you
Walk home instead of going to school
payload.explanation: Counting change and resolving the pass issue later is the practical split — today's journey and tonight's search are separate problems.

payload.snippet: Your younger sibling is refusing to eat breakfast and it is making the whole family late this morning.
options: Tell a parent and focus on getting yourself ready on time
Argue with your sibling to make them eat faster
Skip your own breakfast to wait for your sibling
Start crying because the routine is broken
payload.explanation: Handing the sibling issue to a parent and focusing on your own readiness is the most productive split of effort.

payload.snippet: You cannot remember if you have PE today and your kit is not in your bag.
options: Check the timetable and pack it quickly just in case
Leave the kit and hope you do not have PE
Text a friend to ask while you wait for the answer
Tell the teacher you forgot and accept the consequence
payload.explanation: Checking the timetable takes thirty seconds and packing kit just in case removes all risk.

payload.snippet: You woke up fifteen minutes before the bus with wet hair because you showered the night before and it has dried awkwardly.
options: Style it as quickly as possible and accept that it will not be perfect today
Stay home because your hair looks bad
Shower again and miss the bus
Blow dry it completely and skip breakfast to make up the time
payload.explanation: Accepting a less-than-perfect hair day is the correct morning tradeoff when time is short.

payload.snippet: The cereal box is empty and it is the only breakfast food you normally eat.
options: Check the cupboard for a different option and eat something rather than nothing
Skip breakfast because your preferred food is gone
Wait for your parent to buy more cereal before eating
Go to school hungry and ask a friend for food
payload.explanation: Any breakfast is better than no breakfast — checking for alternatives takes fifteen seconds.

payload.snippet: Your school has sent a reminder that it is non-uniform day today and you completely forgot until this morning.
options: Choose an appropriate outfit quickly from what is in your wardrobe
Wear your uniform and explain you forgot
Stay at home because you have nothing to wear
Text the school to ask if you can wear uniform instead
payload.explanation: A quick wardrobe decision is the correct response to a forgotten non-uniform day — uniform is always a fallback anyway.

payload.snippet: You cannot remember whether you locked the front door after leaving and you are already five minutes into the walk to school.
options: Text a parent to check or turn back only if no one is home to confirm
Turn back regardless to check even though you will be late
Keep walking and worry about it all morning
Assume it is fine because you usually lock it
payload.explanation: A text or call check takes ten seconds and confirms the answer without necessarily requiring you to turn back.

payload.snippet: The morning news is reporting heavy traffic on the road your parent drives you to school on.
options: Tell your parent early so they can choose a different route or plan
Wait until you are stuck in traffic to mention it
Ask your parent to drive a different way without explaining why
Take the bus instead without telling your parent
payload.explanation: Early information allows a route decision before the car has moved — announcing it in traffic is too late.

payload.snippet: You feel a sore throat coming on but it is a normal school day and you have no temperature.
options: Go to school and mention it to your parent when you get home if it gets worse
Refuse to go to school because of a sore throat
Take cold medicine from the cabinet without telling your parent
Ask your teacher to send you home when you arrive
payload.explanation: A sore throat without a temperature is not normally a reason to miss school — monitoring it is the right response.

payload.snippet: Your water bottle is empty and you forgot to refill it last night before bed.
options: Fill it at the tap in the next two minutes before you leave
Go to school without a water bottle
Buy a bottle of water on the way which costs money every day
Wait until school and use the water fountain all day
payload.explanation: Filling it quickly at home is both free and faster than any alternative.

payload.snippet: You and your sibling both need help from your parent at the same time and your parent is getting the baby ready.
options: Deal with what you can yourself and wait for a genuine blockage
Demand your parent helps you first
Give up on your morning routine entirely
Wake the other parent to get both children sorted at once
payload.explanation: Handling what you can independently before asking for help reduces the morning bottleneck.

payload.snippet: The school gate opens at 8:45 and you arrived early at 8:30 and there is nowhere to wait under cover in the rain.

Stand in the rain for fifteen minutes
Go home and come back at 8:45
Knock on the school door and demand early entry
payload.explanation: Using nearby shelter is the obvious and free solution to waiting in the rain.

payload.snippet: You have a maths test first period and you realise you left your revision notes at school yesterday.

Stay home to avoid the test
Ring the school to ask if someone can read you the notes
Blame the teacher for not letting you take notes home
payload.explanation: A quick mental review of what you already know is productive in the time available — the notes are gone and the test is not.

payload.snippet: Leo's mum packed a sandwich but he does not like it.

throws it in the bin
refuses to eat at all
demands a new one now
payload.explanation: Swapping is a polite solution that means neither child wastes food.

payload.snippet: Mia opens her lunchbox and finds her yogurt has leaked all over.

throws everything away
leaves the whole mess there
cries and goes hungry
payload.explanation: Cleaning up the spill and eating the salvageable food is the best approach.

payload.snippet: Kai forgot to put his lunch in his bag before school.

skips eating for the day
steals another child's food
calls home to complain
payload.explanation: Borrowing a school lunch is the practical solution to a forgotten lunch.

payload.snippet: Nina finds her apple has a small brown bruise on one side.

throws the whole apple away
refuses to eat any fruit
cries about her ruined lunch
payload.explanation: A small bruise does not make an apple unsafe — you can eat around it.

payload.snippet: Tom's soup spilled inside his bag on the way to school.

hides the bag and says nothing
blames the soup flask brand
goes home early for a clean bag
payload.explanation: Telling a teacher means you get the right help to clean up and find food.

payload.snippet: Ava forgot to bring her water bottle to school today.

cries until a teacher gives her one
payload.explanation: Drinking from a water fountain is the simple solution to a forgotten bottle.

throws the whole sandwich away
demands his mum bring a new one
goes home for the day

payload.snippet: Grace packed cold leftover pasta and hopes it still tastes nice.

throws it all away uneaten
trades her whole lunch away
payload.explanation: Eating cold leftovers is perfectly fine and wastes nothing.

refuses to eat his own food

payload.snippet: Lily dropped her fork and it now has dirt on it.

refuses to eat at all
payload.explanation: Getting a clean fork is the hygienic and sensible solution.

payload.snippet: Zoe's sandwich bag is very tricky and hard to open today.

asks the teacher to open it

shouts at the other child

tells everyone her mum is silly

throws the entire lunchbox away
demands the school give him new crisps
cries about his ruined snack

payload.snippet: Sophie spills her juice box all over the lunch table.

pretends the spill did not happen
payload.explanation: Cleaning up your own spill is the responsible thing to do.

demands his mum bring new crackers
throws away all his food
payload.explanation: Crumbled crackers are still fine to eat — shape does not matter.

tells the teacher she is starving
refuses to eat the small snack
payload.explanation: Eating what you have and waiting until home is the right response.

refuses it loudly in front of class
payload.explanation: Trying a small bite before deciding is the fair and adventurous thing to do.

payload.snippet: Isla forgot to pack her dessert even though she made it last night.

refuses to eat her main lunch at all
payload.explanation: Calmly telling your mum later is the mature response to a small mistake.

waits for someone else to deal with the fallen bag

stays on the bus all the way to the final stop
calls his mum in a panic while the bus is still moving

shouts at people in front to move faster
gives up and decides to walk the entire way

says nothing and hopes his bag is still there later
blames his friend for not reminding him about the bag

payload.snippet: Grace finds a mobile phone left on the bus seat beside her.

puts it in her bag to use until the owner is found
leaves it on the seat for the next person to deal with

payload.snippet: Max has very smelly trainers and other passengers are noticing.

pretends the smell is coming from someone else
laughs about it loudly with his friends

payload.snippet: Lily sees an older woman struggling to lift her heavy bag to the overhead shelf.

holds the bag but does not actually lift it up
payload.explanation: Offering to help someone who is struggling is a kind and thoughtful action.

payload.snippet: Zoe's friends are playing music on a speaker and other passengers look annoyed.

moves to another part of the bus to distance herself from them

payload.snippet: Sam's bus is running very late and he will miss the start of an important test.

gets off the bus and tries to run to school
demands the driver go faster
cries and says there is no point going to school now
payload.explanation: Contacting a parent to inform the school is the most effective and calm action.

payload.snippet: Finn finds a wallet stuffed with cash on the floor under his seat.

looks through it for a name and calls the owner himself
keeps the cash and hands in the empty wallet
leaves it there since it is not near his own seat
payload.explanation: Handing the wallet to the driver is the honest and correct action.

payload.snippet: Ruby gets on the bus and friends want her to sit with them but there is only one gap.

insists a friend moves to another seat to make a better space
stands in the aisle next to her friends instead of sitting
sits on her own feeling upset rather than choosing
payload.explanation: Joining the group in the available space is the social and practical solution.

payload.snippet: Owen is on the bus when a stranger starts asking him personal questions about where he lives.

answers all the questions honestly to seem polite
shouts at the stranger to leave him alone
moves immediately to sit right behind the driver
payload.explanation: Not sharing personal information with strangers is an important safety habit.

payload.snippet: Sophie accidentally steps on someone's foot getting onto the crowded bus.

keeps moving as if nothing happened
says sorry but then laughs about it to her friend
blames the crowd for making her trip
payload.explanation: Apologising and checking the person is not hurt is the caring and responsible action.

payload.snippet: Jake sees the bus driver yawn several times during the long journey.

tells all the other passengers the driver is falling asleep
shouts to the driver trying to keep them awake
asks his friend to film the driver yawning as evidence
payload.explanation: Reporting a concern about driver tiredness to an adult after arrival is the responsible action.

payload.snippet: Chloe is on the bus when a fight breaks out between two teenagers a few rows ahead.

goes over to try to separate the teenagers herself
films the fight on her phone excitedly
shouts at the teenagers to stop arguing
payload.explanation: Staying safe in your seat and alerting the driver is the right response to a conflict.

payload.snippet: Ethan is on the bus and the person next to him falls asleep on his shoulder.

pushes the person off immediately
wakes the person up with a loud noise
moves away leaving them to fall sideways
payload.explanation: Letting a tired person rest without disturbing them is a kind and patient choice.

payload.snippet: Isla gets on the bus and notices the floor is wet and slippery near the entrance.

slips past carefully without saying anything
stands in the entrance blocking everyone while she decides what to do
waits until someone slips and falls before saying anything
payload.explanation: Telling the driver protects all passengers from slipping and is the responsible action.

payload.snippet: A thunderstorm rolls in just as the family finishes setting up the tent for the camping trip.

Stay outside to enjoy the thunder up close
Open the tent flaps for ventilation
payload.explanation: Securing food keeps it dry through the storm.

payload.snippet: Strong winds bend the trees during the school's afternoon outdoor sports practice.
options: Move the equipment to the indoor gym
Continue practice on the open field
Tie all the kids to a tree
Use the wind to throw the ball further
payload.explanation: Indoor sports stay safe in high winds.

Stop watering to test how strong they are

Tilt the head back to enjoy the glare

Stand on the bow to spot the shore

Spray hot water on the lawn

Swim out into the lake

Take it on a long mountain hike

Lock the cage in a dark closet

Hide the chewed shoe in the bin quietly

Put it in with a strange dog
Free it into the garden alone

Spray the kitten with cologne

Wash it in hot water

payload.snippet: The dog has been left at home alone for the first time and barked the whole hour.

Lock it in a tiny crate
Skip walking it for days

Glue the glasses down

Drop it at a kennel forever
Leave it tied outside the new home

options: Listen carefully and follow the new plan

Form your own team only of friends

payload.snippet: A classmate is rude to the cafeteria server during lunch in the school canteen.

payload.snippet: You scored higher than usual on a maths test and a friend looks disappointed.

Sow more wildflower seeds on top

payload.explanation: Propping and assessing first — some crushed plants recover once the weight is off.

Add more compost to the top

payload.explanation: Tight spacing splits the available nutrients between too many competing bulbs.

Plant only water plants in the beds
Leave puddles to drain on their own each time

Add more nitrogen fertiliser immediately
Remove the entire plant and start again
